author: claude

patch.value: The number finding matters more than its severity label suggests. This package exists to be byte-identical with the published CLI, and a hash divergence does not surface as a wrong number, it surfaces as history_drift on someone else's machine days later. It is the same failure class as two CLI versions hashing identically-declared records differently, filed upstream as pm-cli issue 1135.
A float in item metadata hashes differently from the published CLI, and two doc contracts describe behaviour the code does not have

Three findings from CodeRabbit that had no reply. The hash: stable_json rendered numbers with serde_json, which writes a whole-valued f64 as 30.0 where JSON.stringify writes 30. Any item carrying a float in its metadata therefore produced a different before_hash and after_hash than the published CLI, which reads downstream as a corrupt history chain rather than as a formatting disagreement. The docs: COMPATIBILITY.md listed create as failing fast on a live lock and not implementing the wait budget, while the supported list above it said every mutation retries the budget and create_item does call acquire_lock with settings.locks. workspace.rs said an update requires at least one field to change, while update_item only tests presence, so setting a field to the value it already holds is accepted and writes a history record.

A whole-valued float and the same integer produce identical document hashes; exponent-form values render as JSON.stringify renders them; the renderer contains no unreachable branch; COMPATIBILITY.md no longer contradicts itself about the create lock wait budget; the update docstring states presence rather than change; coverage stays at 100 percent on every metric.

value.author: claude
value.text: Non-vacuity at the digest level: removing the Value::Number arm makes a whole-valued float and the same integer hash to 1517ee47... and 61849ffe... respectively; restoring it makes them identical.

value.author: claude
value.text: Measured against node: JSON.stringify(30.0) is 30,JSON.stringify(1e21) is 1e+21,JSON.stringify(1e-7) is 1e-7. serde_json already signs exponents identically,so only the whole-valued case diverges and an exponent branch would have been unreachable code dressed as a safeguard.

author: claude

patch.value: stable_json routes Value::Number through javascript_number, which renders a finite whole-valued float below 1e21 without a decimal point and leaves everything else to serde_json, whose exponent form already matches. COMPATIBILITY.md's stale create exclusion is gone and workspace.rs states presence rather than change.
An item carrying a float in its metadata hashes identically on the native and published sides, and both documents describe what the code does.

Removing the Value::Number arm makes a whole-valued float and the same integer hash differently and the test fails; restoring it passes. Gates: cargo fmt --check 0, clippy -D warnings 0, cargo test 139 passed 0 failed, rustdoc with -D missing-docs 0, llvm-cov --branch 100.00 percent regions / functions / lines / branches.

message: Match JSON.stringify number rendering and correct two doc contracts
